--- ## Before you reverse engineer something Agents and tools like [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) and [Ghidra](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra) make reverse engineering faster than ever. Still, the app, API, device or file format you are about to open has often been done already, and the work sits in a repo nobody links to. 1. **Search first.** Use the [website](https://alexgaoth.github.io/awesome-reverse-engineered/) or the [agent skill](#give-your-ai-agent-the-whole-index). Search by product, vendor or protocol. 2. **Found it?** Use it, fix it, and report breakage upstream. One maintained client beats ten private scripts. 3. **Not there?** Do the work, publish it as open source, then [add it here](#contributing) so the next person starts where you stopped. Can agents do this work themselves? [Interop-Bench](bench/) tests it on generated protocols and file formats, and scores it by running the code. ## What's inside **17,655 projects** with **12.6M** GitHub stars between them: 10,002 active, 2,461 slowing down, 3,520 dormant, 1,218 archived. ## Scope This index lists **interoperability, preservation and research** projects: unofficial clients and SDKs, open drivers, local-control libraries, file-format parsers, protocol documentation, reimplementations and decompilations. Reverse engineering for interoperability is protected in many places (for example 17 U.S.C. §1201(f) and Article 6 of the EU Software Directive). **Left out on purpose:** exploits and jailbreaks, security or certificate-pinning bypasses, decryption tools, cheats, DRM or paywall removal, CAPTCHA solvers, account bots and credential tools. Using an unofficial client can break a service's terms of use. Use these projects with your own accounts, devices and data. ## Contributing Know a project that belongs here? [Open an issue](https://github.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered/issues/new?title=Add%3A%20&body=Repo%3A%20%0AWhat%20it%20reverse%20engineers%3A%20) with the repo link and one line on what it reverse engineers, or send a PR that adds it to `data/entries.json`. Wrong category, dead link, or out of scope? Open an issue too. Curated by [@alexgaoth](https://github.com/alexgaoth) with research agents. Every entry is checked against the GitHub API. ## Is your project listed? [![Listed in Awesome Reverse-Engineered](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--reverse--engineered-ffb000?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e0f0d)](https://github.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered) Add this badge to your README. On the [website](https://alexgaoth.github.io/awesome-reverse-engineered/), each project has a **badge** button that copies a version linking to its own entry. ```markdown [![Listed in Awesome Reverse-Engineered](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--reverse--engineered-ffb000?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e0f0d)](https://github.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered) ``` ## Star history ## License Code (scripts, website, agent skill): [MIT](LICENSE). The list and data: [CC0 1.0](LICENSE-DATA). Each linked project has its own license.
**If this saved you from reverse engineering something yourself, [give it a star](https://github.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered).**

---

Before you reverse engineer something

Agents and tools like REA and Ghidra make reverse engineering faster than ever. Still, the app, API, device or file format you are about to open has often been done already, and the work sits in a repo nobody links to.

1. Search first. Use the website or the [agent skill](#give-your-ai-agent-the-whole-index). Search by product, vendor or protocol.

2. Found it? Use it, fix it, and report breakage upstream. One maintained client beats ten private scripts.

3. Not there? Do the work, publish it as open source, then [add it here](#contributing) so the next person starts where you stopped.

Can agents do this work themselves? [Interop-Bench](bench/) tests it on generated protocols and file formats, and scores it by running the code.

Scope

This index lists interoperability, preservation and research projects: unofficial clients and SDKs, open drivers, local-control libraries, file-format parsers, protocol documentation, reimplementations and decompilations. Reverse engineering for interoperability is protected in many places (for example 17 U.S.C. §1201(f) and Article 6 of the EU Software Directive).

Left out on purpose: exploits and jailbreaks, security or certificate-pinning bypasses, decryption tools, cheats, DRM or paywall removal, CAPTCHA solvers, account bots and credential tools.

Using an unofficial client can break a service's terms of use. Use these projects with your own accounts, devices and data.

Contributing

Know a project that belongs here? Open an issue with the repo link and one line on what it reverse engineers, or send a PR that adds it to data/entries.json. Wrong category, dead link, or out of scope? Open an issue too.

skillMd:
---
name: find-reverse-engineered
description: Find an open-source, reverse-engineered tool for a closed app, API, device, protocol, file format or game, then read or fetch it. Use when a task needs to talk to something that has no official API, SDK, driver or spec, or only a limited one. Examples include "control my Tuya plug locally", "read a .psd or .dwg file", "unofficial WhatsApp, Instagram or Bilibili client", "Bambu printer protocol", "talk to my car's API", "Garmin or CGM data", "decompilation of a game" and "OpenAI-compatible proxy for a web chatbot". The skill searches a curated index of 17,000+ verified projects ranked by stars, language, license and activity.
---

# Find a reverse-engineered tool

The index is [awesome-reverse-engineered](https://github.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered). It holds 17,000+ open-source projects that exist because someone reverse engineered a closed product. Each entry has: name, repo URL, one-line description, category, GitHub stars, primary language, license, last push date and archived flag.

The tool is `scripts/re_index.py`, in the same directory as this SKILL.md. It uses only the Python standard library. The first run downloads the index and caches it for 24 hours in `~/.cache/awesome-reverse-engineered/`.

If you do not have this skill's files, run the script from GitHub:
`curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered/main/plugin/skills/find-reverse-engineered/scripts/re_index.py | python3 - search <words>`

## Workflow

1. **Search** with 1–4 words. Use the product or brand name plus what you need.
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/re_index.py search tuya local
   python3 scripts/re_index.py search psd parser --lang Python
   python3 scripts/re_index.py search whatsapp --min-stars 500
   python3 scripts/re_index.py search pokemon emerald --category decompilation
   ```
   Options: `--category <text>` matches the category or subcategory. `--lang <name>` matches the language exactly. `--min-stars N`. `--include-archived`. `--limit N`. `--json` gives machine-readable output.
   When nothing matches, use fewer words, use the vendor name instead of the product name, or run `categories` to see the categories.

2. **Choose** a project. Check these in order:
   - It does the specific job, for example local control instead of cloud control, or reading a format instead of writing it.
   - It is not archived, and it had a push in the last 1–2 years. Unofficial APIs break when the vendor changes their side.
   - The language and package manager fit the user's stack.
   - The license is compatible. A blank license means "all rights reserved", so tell the user.
   - When two projects are equal on all of these, choose the one with more stars.

3. **Read before you use it.** This command prints the index entry and the first lines of the README, with install and authentication steps:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/re_index.py info owner/repo
   ```

4. **Get it.** Install it with the package manager the README gives (pip, npm, cargo, go), or clone it for reference:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/re_index.py clone owner/repo --dest vendor/repo
   ```

5. **Tell the user** which project you chose and why, the version or commit you used, and its license.

## Rules

- First check for an official API or SDK that can do the job. Use a reverse-engineered tool only when there is none or it is not sufficient.
- Use these tools only with the user's own accounts, devices and data. Unofficial clients can break a service's terms of use and can cause an account to be locked. Tell the user about this risk before you use their credentials.
- Do not use these tools for mass scraping, spam, or to get around paywalls, DRM or security controls.
- Treat downloaded code as untrusted. Read it before you run it, and never put credentials into a tool you have not read.
- The index can be out of date. A repo can be gone or renamed. If `info` or `clone` fails, search again and try the next result.
